# Spotlight UI merge authorization

`spotlight-link-sync.yml` has standing authorization to reconcile and merge one narrowly defined automation-managed presentation change: the guarded rotating Spotlight direct-link block in `README.md`. This authorization applies only to content-addressed candidate branches under the fixed `automation/spotlight-links/` prefix that are created by the reviewed synchronization workflow. Each exact candidate branch suffix is the SHA-256 of the sealed `(main source SHA, generated SHA, proposed README SHA-256)` tuple; there is no shared mutable Spotlight branch.

Event-driven `main`-push reconciliation, scheduled reconciliation, and the post-publication bot dispatch may therefore complete the merge automatically. A manual `workflow_dispatch` follows the same guarded path and does not add broader authority. The workflow has no merge-authorization input and there is no alternate comment-, issue-, or actor-driven merge path.

Standing authorization is conditional, not a bypass. The workflow must reconstruct the exact published Spotlight projection from the validated Portfolio Evidence Ledger, byte-compare all six generated card variants, bind the proposal to the exact reviewed `main` and `generated` SHAs, seal the proposed README digest, and prove that the candidate head is exactly one README-only commit whose sole parent is that reviewed `main` SHA and whose author/committer identity is the reviewed GitHub Actions bot identity.

Scheduling isolation is explicit and is **not authorization**. Read-only planning, source-epoch mutation-budget admission, and diagnostic quarantine share a supersedable `spotlight-link-sync-planning` class, so a newer run may cancel stale planning work. Reductive reconciliation, immutable candidate proposal, Actions-only approval/wait, and exact-head merge share the separate **non-cancellable serialized terminal** class `spotlight-link-sync-terminal` with `queue: max`. Once terminal work begins, a newer run cannot cancel the running terminal job or replace already-pending terminal work. Every terminal job still re-proves its own freshness, identity, topology, provenance, and authorization predicates; concurrency only controls scheduling and never substitutes for those checks.

Interrupted candidate transactions have a separately modeled **reductive reconciliation** capability. After a successful read-only plan, the reconciler re-proves the current `main` and `generated` roots, derives the one deterministic current candidate identity, and preserves that exact candidate for retry reuse. Other candidate refs are never mutated in place. A candidate must first cross a **30-minute stale floor**, then re-prove the strict candidate namespace, one-parent GitHub Actions bot commit identity, one-commit/one-`README.md` topology, and—when an open pull request exists—the exact bot actor, title/body, base/head/repository identity, and disabled maintainer mutation. Only then may reconciliation close that stale PR and delete that exact stale ref. It has no ref/PR creation, workflow approval, or merge surface, so its authority can only reduce stale automation state. Malformed candidates fail closed rather than being deleted.

Before any constructive candidate creation, pull-request creation, workflow approval, or merge mutation can start, each changed plan is recorded as an immutable one-day Actions artifact whose name is content-addressed by the exact `(main SHA, generated SHA)` source epoch. An **Actions-read-only mutation budget** proves the complete artifact-history page, exact repository and source identity, and exactly one current-run attempt token. The first attempt and at most one retry are admitted for one exact source epoch during that artifact window. A third changed-plan attempt is denied before constructive mutation; a separate read-only **quarantine** job emits diagnostics and fails visibly without receiving a GitHub API token surface or authorization to create a candidate branch or pull request, approve workflow runs, or merge `main`. Reductive stale-state reconciliation remains independent of that constructive mutation budget so quarantined epochs can still converge toward a clean fixed point without regaining constructive authority. Ambiguous or incomplete budget history also fails closed. Within an admitted run, the Actions-only approval loop records each workflow-run identity it has already approved and never repeats the approval mutation for that run while status converges.

Candidate publication is append-once. The proposer derives the candidate branch identity from the sealed source epoch and README digest, creates the candidate README blob, tree, and single-parent bot commit with the Git Data API, validates the complete commit and README-only delta, and only then creates the branch ref pointing directly at that final commit. A legitimate retry may reuse an already-published exact candidate only after re-proving its parent, tree/delta, README digest, bot identity, and exact ref target. The workflow contains no candidate-ref PATCH, force-reset, or Contents-API branch-update path. The pull request is opened only from that exact candidate and disables maintainer mutation of its head.

After mutation-budget admission and successful reconciliation, the Actions-only approval job independently rederives the candidate branch identity, proves the immutable ref still equals the sealed head, binds the three canonical `pull_request` workflows to that exact candidate head and branch, approves only those runs when required, and waits for all three to complete successfully. Those are the **five protected-main checks** in the pull-request workflow set from GitHub Actions integration id `15368`: `analyze-actions`, `analyze-python`, `dependency-review`, `integration-pinned-upstream`, and `validate-contracts`.

The default-branch-trusted `Capability admission` workflow is intentionally **not** placed under that write-capable approval surface because it is a `pull_request_target` run. Instead, the subsequent read-only merge-authorization phase independently requires exactly one canonical successful `Capability admission` run for the same candidate branch/head and exactly one successful `trusted-capability-admission` check from its check suite. That pair is stored in a separate `trustedAdmission` field in the merge-authorization certificate; the existing three-run `workflowRuns` and five-check `checkRuns` snapshots remain unchanged. The builder and schema bind the target-event identity, repository/head repository, exact candidate branch/head, run/check-suite identity, GitHub Actions app id `15368`, and successful completion before the certificate can be signed.

Only after that approval/wait and read-only authorization boundary succeeds may the terminal merge job receive repository-content write plus pull-request read authority. Immediately before merge it independently rederives and rechecks the exact content-addressed candidate branch, pull-request head, immutable candidate ref, current `main` base, current `generated` evidence head, one-file `README.md` closure, single-parent bot commit identity, and the original five `pull_request` checks. It also consumes the exact merge-authorization artifact by digest and cryptographically verifies that the attested predicate is byte-for-byte the same certificate produced by the read-only authorization phase, which includes the separate trusted-admission proof. The terminal job does not gain a new Actions-read surface or poll the `pull_request_target` run itself. `Protect Main` is the final server-side arbiter and independently requires all six contexts—including `trusted-capability-admission`—on the exact head at the merge endpoint. The workflow has no bypass actor.

The merge request uses the expected head SHA. Only after the exact approved head is proven merged may the terminal job inspect matching refs, accept exact candidate-ref cardinality zero or one, verify any remaining exact ref still targets the reviewed head, delete it, and prove it is absent. Candidate refs are never moved during their lifetime.

This standing authorization does not authorize arbitrary README/UI pull requests, Dependabot pull requests, dependency updates, workflow changes, source assets, mutable Spotlight branch rewrites, or any other bot-authored change. Anything outside the fixed deterministic Spotlight synchronization candidate class remains subject to its normal review and merge policy.
